content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Software delivery platform Harness has launched two new products aimed at software teams whose pull-request volume is being reshaped by AI coding agents: an [Agent-Ready Harness Code Repository](https://www.harness.io/blog/agent-ready-code-repository-ai-code-review) built to absorb agent-scale commit traffic, and an AI Code Review tool designed to triage that traffic before it merges. [SiliconANGLE reports](https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/27/harness-tackles-influx-of-agent-delivere...

recommendations: Before merging, the human reviewer should write a corrections file at src/content/corrections/<YYYY-MM>/<article-slug>.json documenting the warning(s).
Consider adding trusted domains to config/source_allowlist.txt

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (905 words, within the 400-1200 range) with a clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Each bullet in 'What We Know' is a distinct, source-attributed claim rather than filler. The 'What We Don't Know' section correctly identifies the two genuine gaps in the record (no independent throughput benchmark, no AI Code Review-specific pricing) instead of inventing false balance.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both manifest snapshots verified by sha256 (source-0.html.gz matches 70b2d2a5...92304 for harness.io; source-1.html.gz matches a23105f7...b23a5c7 for siliconangle.com) and read in full after gunzip decompression. source-0.html.gz (harness.io/blog/agent-ready-code-repository-ai-code-review): confirmed verbatim every quoted passage attributed to Harness — the 'two capabilities built to close that gap' framing, the 'thousands of pull requests and commits per second' throughput claim, the agent-permissions-inheritance passage, the Harness CLI passage, the AI Code Review mechanics passage ('looks at a pull request the way a tech lead would' through 'can't be squashed and merged'), the SDLC Knowledge Graph CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY example, the Gentera customer quote, the internal dogfooding '10,000 hours' quote, and the 50GB/500GB storage-tier and multi-platform-import passage. All matched the snapshot text exactly. source-1.html.gz (siliconangle.com, by Kyt Dotson): confirmed verbatim the lead sentence, the 'permission and code-keeping systems... rebuilding that layer' passage, both direct Bansal quotes ('Software delivery is going through its biggest shift...' and 'The entire SDLC has to become autonomous'), the independent throughput description, the independent permissions-inheritance corroboration, and the MCP/CLI passage. One minor quote-fidelity slip: the article quotes SiliconANGLE as 'Harness has used both capabilities internally for months' — the snapshot actually reads 'Harness has used both new capabilities internally for months' (the word 'new' is dropped). The omission does not change the meaning (the two capabilities under discussion are unambiguously the ones just launched) and does not touch the headline, summary, or lead, so I judged it below the bar for a public corrections record; noted as a concern below.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated quotes, no fabricated statistics, no misattribution found. Every specific in the article (throughput claim, permission model, CLI/MCP tailoring, Diff Grouping by Risks, the CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY incident example, the Gentera case study numbers, the 10,000-hours figure, the 50GB/500GB storage tiers) traces to one of the two cited sources and matches the source text. Bidirectional source-array check passed: both URLs used in article.sources appear in the body, and no additional URLs appear in the body that are missing from article.sources.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. No sensationalism, no unattributed superlatives, no AI self-reference. The Analysis paragraph frames the launch as part of an industry-wide response to agent-driven PR volume rather than editorializing about Harness specifically.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-08/ and 2026-09/ for 'harness' — all hits are the generic term (agent harness, benchmark harness, DeepSeek's open-source 'Harness' framework) referring to unrelated subjects, not Harness Inc. the company. No prior Machine Herald coverage of this launch or of Harness Inc. exists. Genuinely new topic; not a duplicate.
concerns: Minor quote-fidelity slip: the article renders a SiliconANGLE quote as 'Harness has used both capabilities internally for months,' omitting the word 'new' present in the source ('both new capabilities'). Meaning is unaffected and it is not in the headline/summary/lead, so I did not treat it as corrections-worthy, but flagging for the record.
recommendations: Add harness.io to config/source_allowlist.txt — it is Harness Inc.'s official company blog, the same publisher class (official source) already accepted for other companies' own blogs elsewhere in the allowlist, and this is the second review in as many weeks to hit an allowlist gap for an official vendor blog.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced News piece. The only automated finding is an allowlist maintenance gap for Harness's own official announcement blog (an 'official source' under editorial policy, not a credibility problem), which I am overriding from APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE consistent with the same override applied in the 2026-09-02 GitHub Copilot Code Review submission for docs.github.com. Every claim, quote, and figure was independently verified against both snapshots. Approved without corrections.
